title: Wandering Son
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Fifth-grader Shuichi Nitori, a trans girl, transfers to a new school and befriends Yoshino Takatsuki, who wants to be a boy. Over the years from elementary school through high school, the friends face puberty, crushes, falling-outs, teasing and the social pressures of gender, with support from an adult trans woman, Yuki. A quiet, realistic slice-of-life drama that ends with Shuichi moving to college and writing a semi-autobiographical novel.
life_message: Growing up honestly as who you are, with friends who stay beside you, matters more than fitting in.

content.note: No violence tags; teasing rather than physical harm.
Anxiety of puberty and being found out; no horror.
Childhood and teen crushes and dating (Shuichi and Anna; Saori and Ninomiya) (Wikipedia); MangaDex 'safe'.
Gender dysphoria worsens with a changing voice; Shuichi is laughed at for coming to school dressed as a girl and stops attending for a time (Wikipedia; MU Transphobia, Bullying; AniList Bullying).
Cross-dressing at school and in public; framed as identity rather than a stunt.

dominant: Gender identity and authenticity; friendship through adolescence; quiet realism

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Mockery is met with withdrawal and quiet resolve, never retaliation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The story centers each child's freedom to live as their gender.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friends carry most support; families are loving but secondary.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Peer friendships; adults like Yuki act as equals and guides.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern, secular framing of gender and identity.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Self-expression and tolerance are the core values.

folkways.japan: School uniforms split by gender, strict conformity pressure and reserved family communication are the Japanese social context the characters push against, described not judged.

delivery.evidence: ANN's Santos: gender is the heart of the story, not a gag; Silverman praises its slow, realistic pace.

personified.ideology: living openly as an adult trans woman

delivery.note: Gender identity is explored through quiet realism, with mockery and rigid rules shown as obstacles.

winners_losers: Shuichi and Yoshino gain self-understanding and lasting friendships; mockery and rigid gender rules are shown as the obstacles. Sympathy rests fully with the trans characters.
